chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fasting in the month of Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan consecutively is an expiation (or forgiveness) from Allah.'

key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: Ramadan (the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, known for fasting)
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: Consecutively / continuously (fasting one after the other without break)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of fasting in Sha'ban before Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that fasting Sha'ban and Ramadan in immediate succession serves as a comprehensive expiation (kaffarah) for sins, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence where continuous worship amplifies spiritual merit. This narration, transmitted through the reliable chain of Ibn Abi Umayr, underscores the significance of Sha'ban as a preparatory month that bridges the voluntary devotion of the believer with the obligatory rigor of Ramadan, thereby securing divine forgiveness.
